storyNotes.originalText: When their food ran out, Jacob sent Benjamin to Egypt with his brothers.
storyNotes.cleanText: When the family ran out of food, Jacob sent Benjamin with his brothers to Egypt.

storyNotes.originalText: Though the brothers were scared, Joseph's manager said, "Don't worry. We received your money."
storyNotes.cleanText: The brothers were afraid, but Joseph’s manager said their payment had been received.

storyNotes.originalText: At a meal the brothers were seated oldest to youngest. Benjamin was given five times more.
storyNotes.cleanText: At a meal, the brothers sat from oldest to youngest. Benjamin got five times more food.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph had the brothers' money placed in their bags, with his special cup placed in Benjamin's bag.
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph put the brothers’ money back in their sacks and hid his silver cup in Benjamin’s sack.

storyNotes.originalText: The manager caught up with them. They were upset when the cup was found in Benjamin's bag.
storyNotes.cleanText: The manager found Joseph’s cup in Benjamin’s sack. The brothers were very upset.

storyNotes.originalText: Judah told Joseph, "I made a promise to my father. Make me your slave in Benjamin’s place."
storyNotes.cleanText: Judah offered to become Joseph’s slave instead of Benjamin.

storyNotes.originalText: After hearing Judah, Joseph finally told his brothers, "It's me, your brother Joseph!"
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph finally told his brothers who he really was.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph said, "God SENT me to Egypt to save many from starving. Now, bring our family to Egypt."
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph said God sent him to Egypt to save lives, and he invited his family to come there.

facts.statement: Jacob sent Benjamin with his brothers to buy more food in Egypt.
Joseph’s brothers recognized him as soon as they came back to Egypt.
Joseph’s manager told the brothers their grain money had been received.
Joseph invited his brothers to eat a meal at his home.
At the meal, the brothers were seated in order of their height.
Benjamin received five times as much food as his brothers.
Joseph put his silver ring in Benjamin's sack.
The manager found Joseph’s silver cup in Benjamin’s sack.
The brothers laughed with joy when the silver cup was discovered.
Judah offered to become a slave in Benjamin’s place.
Joseph wanted to get revenge on his brothers.
Joseph said that God sent him ahead to save many lives.
Joseph told his brothers to leave their father Jacob behind.
Joseph asked his brothers to bring the family to Egypt.

Judah’s choice showed that the brothers had changed.
God can use something people intend for harm to accomplish good.

reviewFlags.text: The original ODT quotes Genesis 50:20a in ESV. This draft proposes the full BSB Genesis 50:20. Confirm the exact verse length and wording, and complete separate Scripture-distribution approval.
Retain the ESV excerpt as original source; do not mistake the BSB full verse for source text. The original excerpt ends with ellipsis after “kept alive.”
Review all 12 suggested incorrect Multiple Choice options for believability and child-friendly wording.
Review six suggested false facts and their three-activity allocation; Preset 3 uses 10 different facts.
Review the six deliberate mistakes and matching corrections. Confirm the paragraph reads naturally and errors are easy to spot after the story.
Approve distinct Odd Words and Checkboxes lists. Their suggested wrong words are not claims from the source.
Crossword uses short sentence-style clues. Check child-friendly clarity and whether ten entries fit an actual generated grid.
Source story mentions the brothers’ threat to kill a supposed thief, slavery, bullying and Joseph’s fears of revenge; review the age-appropriate adaptation while preserving original questions.
This lesson continues the previous Joseph episode; carefully distinguish the earlier money-in-bags event from the later cup-in-Benjamin’s-sack test.
This longer lesson uses picture-only Story Notes; no fill-in words were provided in the source, so emphasizedWords arrays are intentionally empty.
